[Sat 2026-04-04 09:19 UTC] What are some ideas for hobbies for birdwatchers who want to meet people who aren't birders? Don't use related hobbies, like butterfly raising or building nest boxes, but do make sure the hobbies have at least some outdoors aspect. Put the list in order of most expensive start-up cost to least expensive and include the estimated cost. Don't use a bulleted or numbered list.

**IMPORTANT**: Write your response to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.

arguments.content:
Sailing with a cruising or day-sail boat — Estimated startup cost: $8,000 (club initiation + lessons or a used small boat + basic gear). Getting involved in a sailing club or crewing on other people's boats gets you on the water regularly, puts you in social crews and regattas full of people who aren’t birders, and keeps most activity outdoors (harbor, coastal sails, on-deck teamwork).

Equestrian / horseback riding (lessons or leasing a horse) — Estimated startup cost: $6,000 (lessons, tack, and a leasing deposit; owning a horse is much more). Riding stables and lesson programs are very social: you meet fellow riders, trainers, and barn volunteers while spending time outdoors on trails or in arenas.

Motorcycle touring and riding groups — Estimated startup cost: $4,000 (used motorcycle, basic protective gear, and licensing). Weekend group rides and touring clubs are strongly social and outdoors-focused — you’ll meet people at rallies, roadside cafés, and scenic route meetups who have different hobbies and backgrounds.

High-end mountain biking (trail riding / enduro) — Estimated startup cost: $2,000 (quality mountain bike, helmet, basic protective gear). Trail centers, guided rides, and local cycling clubs introduce you to active, outdoorsy people who generally aren’t birders and often hang out at trailheads, cafés, and skills clinics.

Skiing or snowboarding (alpine) — Estimated startup cost: $1,500 (skis/board, boots, bindings, and some lessons or a season pass). Ski resorts and local clubs create a social scene on-lift lines, in lesson groups, and in apres-ski spaces; the sport is seasonally outdoors and draws many non-birding people.

Scuba diving (open-water certification + gear) — Estimated startup cost: $1,200 (certification course plus basic regulator/mask/fins or rental deposits). Dive shops, boat trips, and dive clubs are communal; surface briefings, boat rides, and shore entries put you outside and among people who share an interest in the sea rather than birds.

Sea kayaking or touring canoeing — Estimated startup cost: $800 (boat, paddle, PFD, and a skills course or club intro). Paddling groups, club outings, and guided trips are sociable and mostly non-birding; they spend long stretches outdoors on lakes, rivers, or coastal waters and often end with group picnics or gear chat.

Outdoor or landscape photography (workshops and meetups) — Estimated startup cost: $600 (decent used camera or mirrorless body + one lens; phone-based entry can be near-free). Photo walks, workshops, and local meetups attract people interested in scenery, urban scenes, portraits, and travel; outings are outside and provide easy conversation starters unrelated to birdwatching.

Rock climbing (outdoor trad or sport, plus gym training) — Estimated startup cost: $300 (intro course, basic harness/helmet/shoes; gyms often rent the rest). Climbing partners, crag meetups, and gym-to-crag groups are highly social; conversations and partner-belay time keep you outside and connected with non-birding climbers.

Tennis or pickleball (club play and social leagues) — Estimated startup cost: $150 (racquet/paddle, shoes, and club drop-in fees). Courts and community leagues are social, outdoors (or pavilion-covered), and attract people who play for fitness and socializing rather than nature study.

Trail running or organized group hikes (non-birding meetups) — Estimated startup cost: $120 (good trail shoes and basic kit). Running clubs and meetup groups regularly organize outdoor runs and hikes; they’re friendly, varied in participant backgrounds, and focused on exercise and camaraderie instead of wildlife identification.

Community outdoor volunteering (trail maintenance, park stewardship) — Estimated startup cost: $0–50 (work gloves, sturdy boots, and optional tools). Volunteer crews are often composed of local residents, hikers, and outdoor enthusiasts who want to improve public spaces; the work is outside, social, and attracts people from many walks of life rather than fellow birdwatchers.
